Added static evidence accepts readonly input and mutable numeric output. Target linear reading count/output under bounded Number work.

objective: Classify unknown values using fixed runtime category checks without coercion or collection traversal.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Unknown, typeof and Array.isArray remain current safe TypeScript foundations.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Classifying an unknown input is practical preliminary validation work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Primitive versus boxed categories and avoiding coercion transfer to other boundary checks.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A fixed small decision tree suits the foundational unknown lesson.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Finite-only numeric assumptions or coercion can misclassify valid runtime values.

defects: The explanation overclaimed that nothing could be done with unknown before narrowing.
NaN/infinities, boxed values and non-coercion boundaries were not explicit.
A guard classifying only finite numbers passed every old assertion.
rationale: Retain all correct boards and correct the unknown explanation to specifically require checks before property reads/method calls. Define runtime categories for ordinary values without proxies/accessors, including NaN/infinities as primitive numbers, boxed values as other objects and arrays independent of contents. Cases cover all primitive kinds, boxed/native collections and a null-prototype/fake-array-prototype object, a frozen cyclic sparse array, methods that throw if coerced and long text. Added static rejection checks string return. Target constant type/category work independent of collection contents.

objective: Use an unknown-to-User structural guard before returning the complete accepted parsed object.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Unknown and user-defined structural guards remain current TypeScript patterns.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Checking parsed data before property access is practical boundary handling.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Declared property types versus business validation and inherited data transfer to other guards.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Two fields and valid bounded JSON keep the foundational exercise focused.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Unstated finite/own-property rules can falsely reject values the described structural check accepts.

defects: Direct guard inheritance/array behavior and number-type versus business-rule boundaries were unstated.
Accepted parsed objects with extra fields were not fully described in the brief.
An own-properties-only restriction passed all previous direct guard cases.
rationale: Retain all three correct implementations. Explicitly apply the described non-null typeof object and string/number checks to stable data fields, allowing inherited data and arrays with fields under bounded prototype depth. No added finite-age or nonnegative-age business policy: NaN/infinities are numbers. Functions remain excluded by typeof. readUser handles valid bounded JSON and returns the complete accepted parsed object, including extra/literal __proto__ fields; a large exponent can parse to Infinity. Cases cover inherited/null-prototype/array data, boxed-field rejection, fractional/negative/nonfinite age, unchanged frozen data and a larger parsed extra array. Preserve original predicate static proof. Target linear readUser text parsing under bounded depth and constant direct guard checks.
